speaker: Doctor
text: That's an unusual start—I haven't received your symptoms yet. Could you please describe your main complaints, especially regarding fatigue and any skin issues like itching? Also, have you noticed any changes in your urine or stool color?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Given your history of ulcerative colitis and risk factors for exposure, could you describe the color of your urine and stool, and have you noticed any jaundice, dark eyes, or abdominal pain? REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panel, CBC, HBsAg, Anti-HCV.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hemoglobin: 11.5 g/dL, Leukocyte_Count: 7500/mm3, Platelet_Count: 280,000/mm3, Na: 138 mEq/L, K: 4.7 mEq/L, Bilirubin_Total: 1.5 mg/dL, Bilirubin_Direct: 0.9 mg/dL, Alkaline_Phosphatase: 460 U/L, AST: 75 U/L, ALT: 78 U/L, HBsAg: Negative, Anti-HCV: Negative

speaker: Doctor
text: The liver enzymes show a disproportionate elevation in Alkaline Phosphatase compared to transaminases, suggesting cholestasis, but the viral markers are negative. Given your history of Ulcerative Colitis and severe itching, is there a possibility of a primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) workup, or have you noticed any bone pain, night sweats, or unexplained weight loss that might suggest a lymphoproliferative disorder? REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Liver_and_Biliary_Tree, Abdominal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC). The combination of Ulcerative Colitis, severe pruritus, cholestatic liver enzyme elevation, and scleral icterus is highly characteristic of this condition; the imaging will likely confirm the "beaded" appearance of the biliary tree.
